entries.originalText: “My Son, let not the labours which thou hast undertaken for Me break thee down, nor let tribulations cast thee down in any wise, but let my promise strengthen and comfort thee in every event.
entries.modernizedText: “My Son, do not let the labors you have undertaken for Me break you down, nor let troubles cast you down in any way, but let My promise strengthen and comfort you in every event.

entries.originalText: I am sufficient to reward thee above all measure and extent.
entries.modernizedText: I am sufficient to reward you beyond all measure and extent.

entries.originalText: Not long shalt thou labour here, nor always be weighed down with sorrows.
entries.modernizedText: You will not labor here long, nor will you always be weighed down with sorrows.

entries.originalText: Wait yet a little while, and thou shalt see a speedy end of thine evils.
entries.modernizedText: Wait a little longer, and you will see a speedy end to your troubles.

entries.originalText: An hour shall come when all labour and confusion shall cease.
entries.modernizedText: An hour will come when all labor and confusion will cease.

entries.originalText: Little and short is all that passeth away with time.
entries.modernizedText: Everything that passes away with time is small and brief.

entries.originalText: “Do earnestly what thou dost; labour faithfully in My vineyard; I will be thy reward.
entries.modernizedText: “Do earnestly what you do; labor faithfully in My vineyard; I will be your reward.

entries.originalText: Write, read, sing, weep, be silent, pray, endure adversities manfully; eternal life is worthy of all these conflicts, yea, and of greater.
entries.modernizedText: Write, read, sing, weep, be silent, pray, endure adversities courageously; eternal life is worthy of all these struggles and of even greater ones.

entries.originalText: Peace shall come in one day which is known to the Lord; which shall be neither day nor night,(1) but light eternal, infinite clearness, steadfast peace, and undisturbed rest.
entries.modernizedText: Peace will come on one day known to the Lord, which will be neither day nor night,(1) but eternal light, infinite clarity, steadfast peace, and undisturbed rest.

entries.originalText: Thou shalt not say then, Who shall deliver me from the body of this death?(2) nor cry out, Woe is me, for my sojourning is prolonged,(3) because death will be utterly destroyed, and there shall be salvation which can never fail, no more anxiety, happy delight, sweet and noble society.
entries.modernizedText: You will not say then, Who will deliver me from the body of this death?(2) or cry out, Woe is me, for my sojourning is prolonged,(3) because death will be utterly destroyed, and there will be salvation that can never fail, no more anxiety, happy delight, and sweet and noble company.

entries.originalText: “Oh, if thou sawest the unfading crowns of the Saints in heaven, and with what great glory they now rejoice, who aforetime were reckoned by this world contemptibly and as it were unworthy of life, truly thou wouldst immediately humble thyself even to the earth, and wouldst desire rather to be in subjection to all, than to have authority over one; nor wouldst thou long for pleasant days of this life, but wouldst more rejoice to be afflicted for God’s sake, and wouldst esteem it gain to be counted for nought amongst men.
entries.modernizedText: “Oh, if you saw the unfading crowns of the Saints in heaven and the great glory in which they now rejoice, those who were once held in contempt by this world and regarded as unworthy of life, truly you would immediately humble yourself even to the earth and desire rather to be subject to all than to have authority over one. Nor would you long for pleasant days in this life, but you would rejoice more to be afflicted for God’s sake and count it gain to be considered nothing among people.

entries.originalText: “Oh, if these things were sweet to thy taste, and moved thee to the bottom of thine heart, how shouldst thou dare even once to complain?
entries.modernizedText: “Oh, if these things were sweet to your taste and moved you to the bottom of your heart, how would you dare even once to complain?

entries.originalText: Are not all laborious things to be endured for the sake of eternal life?
entries.modernizedText: Are not all difficult things to be endured for the sake of eternal life?

entries.originalText: It is no small thing, the losing or gaining the Kingdom of God.
entries.modernizedText: It is no small thing to lose or gain the Kingdom of God.

entries.originalText: Lift up therefore thy face to heaven.
entries.modernizedText: Therefore lift up your face to heaven.

entries.originalText: Behold, I and all My Saints with Me, who in this world had a hard conflict, now rejoice, are now comforted, are now secure, are now at peace, and shall remain with Me evermore in the Kingdom of My Father.”
entries.modernizedText: See, I and all My Saints with Me, who in this world had a hard struggle, now rejoice, are now comforted, are now secure, are now at peace, and shall remain with Me forever in the Kingdom of My Father.”
